extracted.description: Analysis scope is restricted to the STORM-AI Warmup dataset (version 2) over the 10-day window 2018-10-01 to 2018-10-10.
The target series is Swarm-A's hourly altitude change per hour, derived from POD SP3 data using an Earth radius of 6371.0.

The candidate variable set must cover all available variables from the two specified sources: OMNI2 embedded metrics (solar wind parameters, IMF measurements, geomagnetic indices, proton flux metrics) and Sat_Density (mean atmospheric density near Swarm-A orbit).
Pearson correlation is computed between each candidate variable and Swarm-A's hourly altitude change, and the strongest correlation is selected by absolute magnitude, allowing either sign.
Identify the single variable with the strongest Pearson correlation against hourly altitude change and report its name together with its correlation value.

stored.description: The candidate variable set must cover all available variables from the two specified sources: OMNI2 embedded metrics (solar wind parameters, IMF measurements, geomagnetic indices, proton flux metrics) and Sat_Density (mean atmospheric density near Swarm-A orbit).
acceptanceCriteria: Every available OMNI2 variable covering solar wind parameters, IMF measurements, geomagnetic indices, and proton flux metrics is included as a candidate for correlation.
Sat_Density, the mean atmospheric density near the Swarm-A orbit, is included as a candidate variable.
No candidate variable from the two specified sources is silently dropped from the correlation computation.

stored.description: Pearson correlation is computed between each candidate variable and Swarm-A's hourly altitude change, and the strongest correlation is selected by absolute magnitude, allowing either sign.
acceptanceCriteria: A Pearson correlation coefficient is computed between each candidate variable and the hourly altitude change.
The strongest correlation is chosen by largest absolute correlation value, so a negative correlation wins if its magnitude exceeds all positive ones.

assertions.description: Pearson correlation is computed between each candidate variable and Swarm-A's hourly altitude change, and the strongest correlation is selected by absolute magnitude, allowing either sign.

stored.description: Identify the single variable with the strongest Pearson correlation against hourly altitude change and report its name together with its correlation value.
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one winning variable is identified and reported.
The reported correlation value is rounded to 3 decimal places with its sign preserved.
The reported winning variable and correlation value are consistent with the Pearson correlations computed over the scoped data.

assertions.description: Identify the single variable with the strongest Pearson correlation against hourly altitude change and report its name together with its correlation value.
